sentences.text:
The Food Inspector Corporation of Tirunelveli filed private http://www.judis.nic.incomplaint against one Narayanan and the revision petitioner Sundaramahalingam, under Section 7(ii) and 16 (1)(a)(i) r/w 2(ix)
(k) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 32(e) and (f) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

2.The case of the prosecution/complainant is that on 18.08.2006 at about 12.00 p.m., in East Car Street, Tirunelveli, he saw the first accused Narayanan selling food articles in his shop  Rajagomathi Stores.
The complainant introduced himself as Food Inspector and enquired about the Vaigai Dates sold by Narayanan.
The said Narayanan informed the complainant that he was having with him about 20 packets of Vaigai Dates, each packet containing 500 grams.
Narayanan was having license from the Tirunelveli Corporation to sell the same.
When he was enquired who had supplied those dates, the said Narayanan informed that the dates packets were sold by Annalakshmi Stores.
It is seen that the Annalakshmi Stores was being run by the revision petitioner herein.
The Food Inspector, thereupon, seized the articles and sent them for analysis by the food analyst.
The Analyst submitted a report.

After complying with the formalities under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, the complainant came to the conclusion that the sample was misbranded and not labelled in accordance with Rule 32(e) and (f) of the Prevention of Food http://www.judis.nic.inAdulteration Rules, 1955.

Based on the same, the Food Inspector filed the impugned complaint in S.T.C.No.4743 of 2007 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate No.4,
Tirunelveli.
The accused denied the charges framed against them and claimed to be tried.
The prosecution examined two witnesses and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P22.
On the side of the accused, no evidence was adduced.

The learned trial Magistrate, by Judgment dated 01.03.2011, came to the conclusion that the accused are liable to be convicted for the offence under Section 7(ii) and 16 (1)(a)(i) r/w 2(ix) (k) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 32(e) and (f) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and sentenced them to three months simple imprisonment.
Each of the accused were levied with fine of Rs.500/-.
It is relevant to note here that in the said Judgment, it was mentioned that the food articles sold by the accused was a good quality article.

Aggrieved by the Judgment passed by the trial Magistrate, the petitioner herein- Sundaramahalingam filed Criminal Appeal No.70 of 2011 before the Additional Sessions Court, Fast Track Court-II, Tirunelveli.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Court, Fast Track Court-II, Tirunelveli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By Judgment dated 04.08.2011, the Appellate Court dismissed the appeal and confirmed the Judgment of the trial Magistrate.
Challenging the same, this revision case came to be filed.

3.When the matter was taken up for hearing, the learned http://www.judis.nic.incounsel appearing for the petitioner submitted the only offence said to have been committed by the petitioner was one of misbranding.
If that be so, the Food Inspector, even at the time of seizure of the food articles ought to have issued a notice in Form IV.

Form IV is as under:-
FORM IV To (Name and address of the vendor) .................................................
................................................} Whereas ...................... intended for food which is in your possession appears to me to be adulterated/misbranded.

2

Now therefore under Sub-Section (4) of Section 10 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (37 of 1954), I hereby direct you to keep in your safe custody the said sealed stock subject to such order as my be issued subsequently in relation thereto.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4.In this case, it is beyond dispute that no notice under Form IV issued by the Food Inspector to A1-Narayanan.
Instead only the notice in Form VI was issued.
Form VI is issued when a food article has to be analysed by the public analyst.
As rightly http://www.judis.nic.in pointed out by the learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner, misbranding of label does not require public analyst's opinion.

It was held in the decision reported in 2009 (2) MWN (Cr.) 446 (P.Robert Immanuel and another Vs. The Sate Represented by the Food Inspector, Alwarthirunagari Town Panchayat at Government Primary Health Centre, Thenithirupperai, Thoothukudi District) as follows:
14.The said Private Complainant has only relied on the Public Analyst report for misbranding of the label.

entities.text: 2009 (2) MWN (Cr.) 446 (P.Robert Immanuel and another Vs. The Sate
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As stated earlier misbranding of label require Public Analyst opinion and the Food Inspector, who had drawn samples had not mentioned anything about the label of beverage bottles.
It is pertinent to note that the beverage is not adulterated but did not contain those particulars as stated earlier which are contemplated under Rules 24,32 and 42.
The petitioner is a petty vendor who sold a beverage of local made.
The manufacturer could not be found by the respondent but the vendor has been proceeded for offences of misbranding as the label of the bottle did not contain so many particulars.

In my considered view, the petitioner is not liable to be prosecuted as Food Inspector who had the occasion to see the beverage bottle did not mention anything about the misbranding and it does not require the opinion of the Public Analyst.
http://www.judis.nic.in
5.Further
, to strengthen his case, the petitioner's counsel also took me to the answers given by P.W.1 in the cross examination.
P.W.1 in the cross examination had stated that when the dates packets were seized, the Accused No.1 was not informed that on the label, the packing date is not mentioned.
In Form VI, no endorsement was taken from A1 that the packing date is not mentioned.
It was further admitted by P.W.1 that when A2 sold the food article to A1, the date of manufacture was written.

sentences.text: 6.The offence of misbranding can be said to be committed only if the label is not in accordance with the requirements of the Act or Rules framed there under.

Rule 32 (f)
of the Prevention of the Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, states that the date, month and year, in which, the article is manufactured, packed or pre-packed, shall be given on the label.

entities.text: Prevention of the Food Adulteration Rules, 1955
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In this case, P.W.1 himself had admitted that those details were very much given, when A2 sold the food articles to A1.
Thus, the evidence on record indicates that the petitioner herein did not commit the offence with which he was charged.
The Courts below failed to appreciate the answers given by P.W.1 in the cross examination and the fact that notice in Form IV was not issued.
Therefore, the offence of misbranding is clearly not made out.
In this view of the matter, the Judgments of the http://www.judis.nic.inCourts below are set aside.
This criminal revision case is allowed.
The petitioner is acquitted.
The fine amount, if any, paid by him shall be refunded forthwith.
The bail bond, if any, executed by the revision petitioner shall stand cancelled.
